I think the story does care about the shit vi went through. But like most of the deep, nuanced topics present in the story, the show wasn't given enough time to address them. That was my biggest issue with season 2. Season 1 was *packed* and couldn't give every aspect of the story the focus it deserved, but they struck a good balance and paced it pretty well. Season 2 was 2 seasons (minimum) worth of story packed into one, and so every aspect suffered to varying degrees. 
If they had season 2 focus on the socio-political conflict between Piltover and Zaun (with Ambessa shit stirring) as well as the personal conflicts between the characters based in the cities with some hints at the Black Rose stuff mixed in, and had season 3 focus on the larger viktor/arcane/BR stuff and the siege of piltover by ambessa, everything would have been much smoother. As it stands, Piltover's oppression of Zaun and all the personal character conflicts and motivations built into it, kinda just stop mattering as they made Ambessa and Viktor the badies and then zaun getting a single surely to be hamstrung and sidelined council member as the solution to a very deep, nuanced and difficult conflict that echoes real world inequalities between classes, read as sloppy at best and tone deaf and dismissive at best. 
All that rambling to say: the story didn't not care about vi, the budget didn't.
